consumed.resolution: console lane cl-skills-drift (fix/skills-drift-worktree-generator): skillsDriftCheckDefault runs the worktree's own evolve skills check (core.WorktreeEvolveInvocation) when the lane changes go/internal/skillcheck/, else skillcheck.Check in-process with byte-identical output; acceptance tests TestSkillsDriftGate_* and the cycle-1840 replay; follow-up skills-drift-gate-generator-dependency-closure

fix: When the lane diff touches go/internal/skillcheck/** (the generator), grade drift with the worktree's own generator (build or run the worktree's `evolve skills check`), not the orchestrator's compiled one. One home for the decision in phases/audit.
source: console, 2026-10-07 cycle 1828 (retro carryover todo-skills-drift-gate-…, promoted to the inbox; the gate-class lane confirmed the version skew)
summary: Cycle 1828 changed the skill-command generator (skillcheck.RenderCommandStub) and regenerated commands/*.md consistently. The audit's in-process skills-drift gate (skillsDriftCheckDefault, go/internal/phases/audit/audit.go:502) renders the expected projections with the generator compiled into the ORCHESTRATOR's (base) binary, so it reported 30 drifted artifacts while the worktree's own build reported none: a false red that overrode an auditor PASS. The gate-class fix (a gate-forced FAIL earns a bounded Build repair and never halts) limits the damage but cannot fix it: the repair rounds re-hit the same skew.
title: The skills-drift gate grades a generator change with the base binary's generator, a false red
